about: A first-person narrator who is a woman, shown only by being addressed as 'ma'am' and called 'Margaret'; no pronoun ever names her gender.
title: The House Above the Valley
author: Ruth Calder

chapters.title: Arrival
paragraphs: I came off the night train with one suitcase and a letter of introduction. The platform was empty except for a porter and a cat.
"Can I take that for you, ma'am?" the porter asked, reaching for the suitcase.
I let him take it. I had carried it for two days and my arm ached from the strap.
Outside the station a man waited beside a black car. He raised his hat when he saw me.
"You must be Margaret," he said. "My name is Tobias, and the house is not far."
I gave him the letter. He read it twice under the lamp and folded it into his coat.
Tobias drove with both hands on the wheel. He did not speak again until the woods.
The road climbed through pine woods. I watched the headlights sweep the trunks and counted the bends.
"Hang on, Margaret, this next turn is a bad one," Tobias said.
I held the door handle and said nothing. The car swung round the bend and the house appeared above us.
Tobias stopped the car at the gate. He got out and pushed it open with both hands.
It was larger than I had imagined. Every window on the ground floor was lit.
Tobias carried the suitcase up the steps. He set it down by the door and wished me good night.
"Welcome home, ma'am," said the housekeeper at the door, and I almost laughed at the word home.
I followed the housekeeper up the stairs. My room looked out over the valley, and I stood at the window until the lights went out below.
